summary: SCIM upsert conflict during provisioning causes group->role bindings to drop for private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a scheduled SCIM provisioning run, a subset of users lost RBAC bindings in their private deployment. Affected users receive 403 when calling the private API even though they are still present in the IdP and in Redwood's user list. The drop appears intermittent and only affects groups that are provisioned via SCIM upsert (PATCH) sequences from the customer's IdP.

Impact:
- Multiple product teams at Knex Analytics unable to access model endpoints behind the private VPC.
- Several users report 403s for routine calls; customer is on a paid private plan and requires immediate mitigation.

Environment:
- Private control plane (customer-managed VPC) running agent v1.37.4
- Region: eu-west
- IdP: Okta acting as SCIM provisioning source

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Provision a new group in Okta with displayName "knex-analytics:research" and externalId "grp-334".
2) In a follow-up sync Okta sends a PATCH (SCIM upsert) with the same displayName but externalId "grp-334​" (zero-width char inserted).
3) Redwood SCIM client receives 200 for the PATCH but the provisioning engine later shows the group as "unbound" to the corresponding role mapping.
4) Users in that group get 403 on calls to private endpoints.

Observed behavior:
- SCIM logs show upsert sequences succeeded with HTTP 200/204 but reconciliation marks the group as duplicate and it is omitted from the role-mapping index.
- When support triggers a manual re-sync in the console the missing bindings reappear and users regain access.

Expected behavior:
- Upserts should be idempotent and preserve role bindings even when small metadata differences (e.g., invisible unicode characters) exist.

Additional context:
- Customer says the issue started after an Okta change that introduced a migration script; they suspect the script added non-printing characters to externalId in some groups.
- No other customers have reported identical failures but one internal customer ticket (INT-4102) shows a similar reconcile edge-case in staging.

Relevant log snippets (redacted):
- "2026-03-11T08:14:22Z scim-client: PATCH /Groups/grp-334 200"
- "2026-03-11T08:14:22Z provisioner: reconcile: found duplicate key 'knex-analytics:research' -> skipping binding"
- "2026-03-11T08:14:23Z rbac: lookup failed for group id 'grp-334​' -> normalized lookup returned null"
comments: 2026-03-11 - Priya Desai (Support): Acknowledged. Asked customer to share SCIM webhook payloads and last successful sync time. Escalated to SRE for deep logs.

2026-03-11 - Knex Support Engineer (customer): Provided full SCIM PATCH payloads and Okta migration script excerpt. Highlighted the zero-width char seen only in their export. Link: slack.com/knex/#scim-mig

2026-03-11 - SRE (Alex Kim): Retrieved agent logs from private control plane; confirmed duplicate-detection path marked group as duplicate during reconcile. Requested agent debug build to surface normalization steps.

2026-03-12 - Support (Priya): Ran manual re-sync via Console for customer which restored bindings for the impacted groups. Recommended a temporary workaround (manual re-sync) while engineering investigates permanent fix.

2026-03-12 - Engineering (Rohit Malhotra): Reproduced locally with a test payload that included U+200B (zero-width space). Filed PR (see related_github_prs) to normalize group identifiers during SCIM upsert handling.
investigation_notes: Root cause hypothesis: SCIM upsert sends logically identical identifiers but with non-printing unicode differences. The provisioning engine's duplicate detection compares displayName/externalId without normalization, causing 'duplicate' label in the index and subsequent omission from role-binding reconciliation.
Confirmed reproduction: Added U+200B into externalId in a staging Okta export; provisioning observed same behavior (200 responses, but reconcile omitted binding).

Edge case: SCIM client reports HTTP 200/204 so upstream looks healthy; error is in downstream reconciliation logic which treats de-duplicated entries as intentionally removed rather than normalized duplicates.
Related internal ticket: INT-4102 documents a similar reconcile edge-case on a non-production cluster using different unicode variations.
Telemetry: No increase in 5xx, but jump in 'rbac_missing_binding' events for customer-specific tenant id.
resolution: Workaround (customer-facing): Run a manual 'Reconcile groups' from the Redwood Console for the affected tenant; this will normalize and reattach missing bindings. Support performed this on 2026-03-12 and customer confirmed access restored.
Temporary mitigation (recommended): Instruct IdP admin to run a cleanup script to strip non-printing unicode from externalId/displayName fields prior to provisioning.

Permanent fix: Engineering merged normalization patch to SCIM upsert pipeline to trim and NFC-normalize identifiers (PR linked). Patch will be released as agent v1.38.1; rollout plan targets private agents first and then hosted fleet.

Post-deploy follow-up: Add an automated 'fuzzy-check' during reconcile to detect and reconcile probable unicode-only differences and surface warnings in the console. Create postmortem entry and update SCIM runbook.
